title: CT angiography
what: A CT scan of your blood vessels. Contrast dye is injected into a vein, and the machine takes pictures that show how blood flows through your vessels.
why: To check the blood vessels of the heart, head, neck, lungs, legs, or the aorta: to find narrowing, a blockage, or a bulge.
duration: usually 15 to 30 minutes with preparation; the scan itself takes a few minutes
tell_doctor: Allergies to contrast dye, iodine, or any medicines
Diabetes and your diabetes medicines. The doctor decides if anything needs to change

prepare.title: Blood test
prepare.text: You are usually asked to do a creatinine test beforehand. This blood test shows how well your kidneys work.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food for 2 to 4 hours before the scan. Your clinic will give you the exact time.

prepare.title: Water
prepare.text: Plain water is usually fine, and even helpful. It helps the dye leave your body faster.

prepare.title: Heart
prepare.text: If your heart vessels are checked, you are usually asked to skip coffee and strong tea that day. Sometimes you get a medicine to slow your pulse, so the pictures are clearer.

steps: A nurse puts a cannula into a vein in your arm
You lie down on the scanner table
Contrast dye is injected through the cannula
The table moves through the ring of the machine
You are asked to hold your breath for a few seconds and stay still
feel: When the dye goes in, you may feel a wave of warmth through your body
Sometimes it feels like you need to pee. This feeling passes quickly
You may have a metal taste in your mouth
after: After the scan, you are usually asked to wait 15 to 30 minutes, to make sure you have no reaction to the dye
Drink extra water that day, unless your doctor says otherwise
The report is usually ready within 1 to 2 days
red_flags: Rash, itching, a swollen face or lips, or trouble breathing: tell staff right away or call emergency services
Strong swelling, pain, or redness where the needle was

faq.a: Most people handle it well. Allergy is rare, so it is important to tell your doctor about allergies and kidney disease beforehand.

faq.q: How is CT angiography different from regular coronary angiography?
faq.a: In CT, a cannula goes only into a vein in your arm, and the machine takes the pictures. In coronary angiography, a thin tube is passed through an artery to the heart.

reminders.text: CT angiography tomorrow. Bring your creatinine result, referral, and medicine list.
Usually no food from now until the CT scan. Plain water is fine. Follow the exact time your clinic gave you.
